description: Models Collatz iteration as a biased random walk on log-space, where odd steps multiply by ~3/2 and even steps divide by 2. The Lagarias-Weiss heuristic predicts max(trajectory) ~ n^2 for starting value n. This stochastic framework yields closed-form predictions for delay distributions.
mathematical_formalization: Let X_k = log_2(T^k(n)). At each step, X_{k+1} = X_k - 1 with prob ~1/2 (even), or X_{k+1} = X_k + log_2(3/2) with prob ~1/2 (odd). Expected drift: mu = (1/2)(-1) + (1/2)(log_2(3/2)) ≈ -0.2075. Variance: sigma^2 ≈ 0.52. Delay ~ |X_0|/|mu| + O(sqrt(|X_0|/sigma)).
analogical_connections: Brownian motion with drift in physics
Random walk on energy landscapes in protein folding
implementation_hypothesis: Build a Monte Carlo simulator that generates synthetic Collatz-like trajectories using the stochastic model. Compare predicted delay distributions with actual Collatz delays to identify anomalous numbers (those deviating significantly from prediction). These anomalies are candidates for delay records.
experiment_seed: Generate 10M random numbers, compute actual vs predicted delay. Rank by (actual_delay - predicted_delay) / predicted_stddev to find statistically anomalous high-delay numbers.

description: Uses evolutionary algorithms to breed starting numbers with high Collatz delay. Numbers are represented as bitstrings; crossover splices binary representations, and mutation flips bits. Fitness = delay(n) / log2(n), normalizing for number size. Inspired by biological evolution optimizing fitness landscapes.
mathematical_formalization: Population P = {n_1, ..., n_K}. Fitness f(n) = delay(n) / ceil(log_2(n)). Selection: tournament of size t. Crossover: single-point on binary representation. Mutation: flip bit i with probability p_mut. Elitism: keep top e individuals. Iterate until convergence or budget exhaustion.
analogical_connections: Natural selection optimizing phenotype in fitness landscapes
Protein sequence evolution under selection pressure
implementation_hypothesis: Implement a genetic algorithm in Python where each individual is an integer. Use bit-level crossover and mutation. Track the Pareto frontier of (bit_length, delay) pairs. After convergence, verify that discovered numbers genuinely have high delay relative to their size.
experiment_seed: Run GA with population 1000, 500 generations, bit-lengths 40-80. Compare best found delay/bit ratios against known records.

description: Uses Kolmogorov complexity intuition to sieve for high-delay Collatz numbers. Numbers with low descriptive complexity (highly structured binary representations) tend to have predictable trajectories. High-delay candidates should have intermediate effective complexity — structured enough to avoid quick convergence but not so random as to follow the mean.
mathematical_formalization: Effective complexity C_eff(n) = K(n) - K(regularity(n)). For Collatz, regularity relates to the distribution of odd/even steps. Target: numbers n where H(bits(n)) ≈ 0.6-0.8, avoiding both perfectly structured and perfectly random patterns.
analogical_connections: Edge of chaos in cellular automata (Langton's lambda)
implementation_hypothesis: Sieve numbers by computing the compressibility of their binary representation (using zlib). Numbers in the 'Goldilocks zone' of compressibility are candidates for high delay. Filter through actual Collatz computation.
experiment_seed: For n in range 2^50 to 2^60, sample 100K numbers stratified by compression ratio. Correlate compression ratio with delay. Identify optimal compression band.

description: Maps the Collatz iteration onto a rugged energy landscape where 'energy' E(n) = -delay(n). Finding high-delay numbers becomes finding deep energy minima. Simulated annealing and basin-hopping algorithms from computational chemistry can navigate this landscape efficiently, escaping local optima.
mathematical_formalization: Energy E(n) = -delay(n). Temperature schedule T(k) = T_0 * alpha^k. Acceptance: P(accept n') = min(1, exp(-(E(n')-E(n))/T(k))). Neighborhood: n' from bit-flips. Basin-hopping: local minimization + random perturbation.
analogical_connections: Spin glass optimization in condensed matter
implementation_hypothesis: Implement simulated annealing where the state is an integer n and moves are bit-flips. The 'energy' is negative delay. Cool slowly to find deep local minima in delay-space.
experiment_seed: Start from known delay records. Perform basin-hopping with 1000 restarts, 10000 steps each. Track whether SA finds higher delay than random search of equal cost.

description: Analyzes binary representations of known Collatz delay records to identify recurring 'motifs' — short binary patterns that appear disproportionately in high-delay numbers, analogous to regulatory motifs in DNA. These motifs guide construction of new high-delay candidates.
mathematical_formalization: Given delay records D = {n_1, ..., n_k}, extract all k-mers from binary(n_i) for k=4..16. Enrichment score: E(motif) = freq_in_records / freq_in_random. Significant motifs have E >> 1 with p < 0.01 by Fisher's exact test.
analogical_connections: Transcription factor binding site discovery in genomics
Crystal structure motifs in materials science
implementation_hypothesis: Convert all known delay records to binary strings. Run motif discovery (analogous to MEME in bioinformatics). Construct new numbers by concatenating enriched motifs. Test their Collatz delay.
experiment_seed: Analyze the ~131 known delay records. Extract 8-bit motifs. Compare frequencies against uniform random. Use top motifs to construct 10000 candidates.

description: Applies renormalization group (RG) ideas from statistical physics to Collatz dynamics. By coarse-graining the trajectory — grouping multiple steps into effective single steps — we identify scale-invariant structure. The Collatz map on residue classes mod 2^k forms a natural RG hierarchy.
mathematical_formalization: Define coarse-grained map T_k: Z/(2^k Z) -> Z/(2^k Z) by iterating T exactly k times on residue classes. Fixed points of T_k correspond to 'self-similar' trajectories. Critical exponents: delay(n) ~ n^gamma near fixed points.
analogical_connections: Kadanoff block spin transformation in Ising model
implementation_hypothesis: Compute T_k for k=1..20. Identify residue classes mod 2^k that produce above-average delays. Numbers in intersection of good classes across scales are prime candidates.
experiment_seed: For k=1..16, compute average delay in each residue class mod 2^k up to 2^30. Identify top 1% classes at each level. Construct intersections.

description: Uses extreme value theory (EVT) to predict the expected delay of the k-th delay record. The GEV distribution fitted to known records forecasts where the next record should fall, and whether any found value is genuinely surprising or merely expected.
mathematical_formalization: Model delay records via GEV: P(D_n <= d) ~ exp(-(1 + xi*(d - mu_n)/sigma_n)^{-1/xi}) where mu_n, sigma_n scale with log(n). Fit xi, mu_0, sigma_0 from known records.
analogical_connections: Record-breaking temperature analysis in climate science
implementation_hypothesis: Fit GEV to known delay records (delay vs log(n)). Predict expected delay of next record. Estimate optimal search range.
experiment_seed: Collect ~131 known delay records. Fit GEV. Compute 95% prediction interval for record #132. Cross-validate by removing last 10.

description: Constructs numbers with provably long odd-step runs by engineering their binary representation. A Collatz trajectory's length is dominated by the ratio of odd to even steps. Numbers whose initial trajectory has unusually high odd-step ratio will have high delay. Connects to large deviations theory.
mathematical_formalization: Collatz on n: if odd, n -> (3n+1)/2^v where v = v_2(3n+1). Trajectory with many v=1 steps grows as (3/2)^k. P(k consecutive odd) ~ (1/2)^k. By large deviations: P(fraction_odd > 1/2 + eps) ~ exp(-n * I(eps)).
analogical_connections: Rare event simulation in computational physics
Extreme weather as large deviation phenomena
implementation_hypothesis: Construct numbers whose binary representation encodes a specific odd/even step pattern using the Chinese Remainder Theorem to force many consecutive odd steps.
experiment_seed: For k=10..30, construct smallest n with k consecutive odd Collatz steps. Measure total delay. Compare against random numbers of same bit-length.

description: The distribution of Collatz delays follows a power law, reminiscent of self-organized criticality (SOC) in sandpile models and earthquake dynamics. This suggests the Collatz system operates near a critical point where scale-free behavior emerges without parameter tuning.
mathematical_formalization: P(delay > d) ~ d^{-alpha} for large d, with alpha ≈ 2-3 (empirical). Analogous to Gutenberg-Richter: P(magnitude > M) ~ 10^{-bM}. The 'avalanche size' in sandpile corresponds to trajectory length.
analogical_connections: Power-law degree distributions in scale-free networks
implementation_hypothesis: Compute delay distribution for n up to 10^8. Fit power law via MLE. Use fitted exponent for importance sampling guided by the power-law tail.
experiment_seed: Compute delays for n = 1 to 10^8. Plot CCDF on log-log. Fit power law tail. Compare exponent with SOC universality classes.

description: Uses LZ-complexity of Collatz trajectories (encoded as binary sequences of odd/even steps) to identify trajectories that are 'algorithmically deep' — requiring many steps to generate despite compressible structure. High logical depth numbers are delay record candidates.
mathematical_formalization: For trajectory tau(n) = (s_1, ..., s_D), s_i in {O, E}, compute LZ-complexity C_LZ(tau). Logical depth delta(n) ≈ D(n) - C_LZ(tau) * log(D(n)). High delta = long but structured trajectory.
analogical_connections: DNA sequence complexity in molecular evolution
implementation_hypothesis: For each candidate n, compute full trajectory, encode as binary (0=even, 1=odd). Compute LZ76 complexity. Rank by delay / LZ_complexity ratio.
experiment_seed: Compute LZ complexity of trajectories for all n up to 10^7. Identify top 0.1% by delay/LZ ratio. Analyze binary representations.

description: Trains a neural network to predict Collatz delay from binary representation of n. Learned features reveal structure invisible to hand-crafted heuristics. Gradient ascent on input space generates candidates, analogous to how AlphaFold learned protein folding.
mathematical_formalization: f_theta: {0,1}^B -> R, f_theta(bits(n)) ≈ delay(n). Architecture: 1D CNN. Loss: MSE. Use grad f_theta w.r.t. input to identify influential bit positions. Generate candidates by gradient ascent on input.
implementation_hypothesis: Train CNN on (binary_representation, delay) pairs for n up to 10^7. Score candidates. Apply gradient-based input optimization. Verify top candidates.
experiment_seed: 1M training pairs. Train CNN. Screen 10M candidates. Compare top 100 predicted vs brute-force top 100.

description: Formulates Collatz delay maximization as a QUBO problem, mapping to quantum annealing language. The QUBO formulation reveals quadratic interaction structure between bits of n that influence delay, enabling classical solvers to exploit this structure.
mathematical_formalization: n as bits x = (x_1, ..., x_B). Approximate delay(n) ≈ sum_i a_i x_i + sum_{i<j} b_{ij} x_i x_j. Maximize QUBO: max_x x^T Q x.
implementation_hypothesis: Fit quadratic model of delay as function of bit variables via LASSO. Solve QUBO exactly for small B, approximately for large B. Compare against random baseline.
experiment_seed: Training data for B=30 bits. Fit QUBO matrix Q. Find maximum. Verify QUBO-optimal x has genuinely high delay.
